## Product Tab

The Product tab under the Product Editor contains non-datetime effective options and is available when users select a product name from the product tree.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 659;height: 486;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Product tab:

- **Fluid Service** - Select a fluid service according to the product. Available options are:
  - Hydrocarbon (default)

  - Nonhydrocarbon

    Selecting "Nonhydrocarbon" will enable the Mass Allowable sub-tab under the Validations tab.

- **Show Uncorrected Density** - Choose whether or not Uncorrected Density should appear on printed tickets. Uncorrected Density is the density before the Density Meter Factor (DMF) is applied.

- **Show Observed Density** - Choose whether or not Observed Density should appear on printed tickets.

- **Show Density Meter Factor** - Choose whether or not the Density Meter Factor should appear on printed tickets.

- **Show Alkenes** - Choose whether or not the product is sampled for alkenes (ethylene, propylene, and butylenes).

  If alkenes and neopentane are disabled here, they will also be disabled for entry on Analysis Entry screens in the Volume Editor, Ticket Editor, Liquid Quality Source, and Standalone Samples when entering data for the given product. These fields will also be suppressed on printed tickets when analysis information is shown. On import of meter, ticket and quality source data, if values are provided for alkenes and neopentane, they will be imported, but an exception will be generated.

- **Show Neopentane** - Choose whether the product is sampled for neopentane. If not enabled, neopentane will be disabled for the Analysis entry.

- **Show -** Determine what to Show on a printed report. When printing a ticket for a product that uses Table E, COSTALD, TP-2 or REFPROP, FLOWCAL shows either the mass percent and component mass, the liquid volume percent and component volumes or both percentages as well as component mass and component volume. That is defined by the following choices:
  - **Use Meter’s Calc. Method** – If the component volumes are calculated using LV% applied to the NSV, then the report displays liquid volume % and component volume on the report. If component volumes are calculated by applying Mass% to the mass to get component mass and then component density is used to get the component volumes, then the report displays mass%, component mass, LV% and component volumes.
  - **Volume** – Always display liquid volume % and component volume on the report.
  - **Mass** – Always display mass % and component mass on the report.

- **Sample Required for Batch Meter** - This option is used to ensure that Batch Meter data with the specified Product has an Analysis applied. If this option is enabled in the Product Editor and there is an LQ Assignment set up on that Meter, then any time data with that Product that is created or edited within the time frame of the LQ Assignment, FLOWCAL validates that there is an Analysis applied to that data. If there is not an Analysis on the Assignment during the data time frame and there is no Sample Override, then FLOWCAL generates exception 18200, LQA - Sample Not Found. Having an Analysis on the Assignment during the time frame, or having a Sample Override on that data keeps the exception from being generated. If the Purity Product is set up in the Product Editor with an Analysis attached, the Analysis applies to the data, but the exception is still not resolved.

  If an LQ Assignment is not set up on the Meter then FLOWCAL does not check whether an Analysis is applied to the data or not. The validation is always looking at the LQ Assignment for an Analysis. Even if the Meter data has an Analysis, if the Assignment does not contain an Analysis for the time frame or a Sample Override is not applied then the exception is still generated.

- **Apply HYC** - When a sample density is provided, it may have been measured with a hydrometer. If the density is not at the base temperature, it needs to have a hydrometer correction applied when calculating base density. There are three options for hydrometer correction in the Product Editor:
  - **None** – No hydrometer correction is needed. The density is either at base temperature, the density is not from a measurement with a hydrometer or the density has already had hydrometer correction applied.
  - **Default Yes** – Typically a hydrometer correction needs to be calculated and applied as part of the base density calculation.
  - **Default No** – Typically a hydrometer correction does not need to be calculated and applied as part of the the base density calculation, but sometimes it will. The user has the option to select when to calculate and apply a hydrometer correction.

- **Sample Required for Standalone Ticket** - This option is used to ensure that any Ticket with that Product has an Analysis. If this option is enabled in the Product Editor, then any Ticket that is created or edited with that Product is checked for an Analysis on that Ticket. If there is not an Analysis on the Ticket, then FLOWCAL generates exception 18200, "LQA - Sample Not Found".

  When FLOWCAL is validating that there is an Analysis on the Ticket, having an S&W%, Mole%, Mass%, or LV% is sufficient enough to keep the exception from being generated. The validation is not run for imported Standalone Tickets.

- **Odorant Allowed** - Hydrocarbons such as propane that are sold for public use are odorized or stenched before being shipped. If a product has odorant added, check Odorant Allowed. This allows for specifying on truck and rail tickets that odorant was added, what the odorant was, and how much odorant was added. Enabling this option also enables the flag on the Accounting tab of the Ticket Editor. If you have a product such as crude oil that is never odorized, then you do not want to enable this option. For a product such as propane which may be odorized before leaving your facility, this option should be enabled.

- **Generate Exceptions for Unavailable S & W % and CSW** - If an S&W value is expected for a product such as crude oil or NGL and the user wants to be alerted via an exception if one is not on the batch, then enable this option.

- **Purity Product** - Setting up a product as a Purity Product has two implications. First, when calculating the sum of component volumes, this value is set to match the Net Standard Volume (NSV) and all component volumes are back calculated from this value using the liquid volume percentages for the sample. Second, the option to assign a default quality source becomes available.

  If no sample is available from a quality source for a batch, then the sample on the default quality source is used. The sample is also automatically applied to tickets with the product unless the ticket belongs to a location with an assigned quality source. This is useful for products such as propane where a sample is not always collected and a standard analysis is assumed.

- **Max component to report** - Analysis on a sample can be done out to C10. When the component volumes are reported on a printed ticket, the product may dictate that everything above a certain component be reported as that component. For instance on propane, analysis may be taken out to C4 for accurate component balancing, but all component volumes will be reported as C3. Setting the max component to report to C3 will cause the component volume from iso-C4 and n-C4 to be reported as C3 component volume. FLOWCAL lumps these values together into a single value for viewing in the Components tab in the volume editor and the ticket editor and also for display on net Allowable ticket reports. Options for Max Component to Report are C2, C3, C3H6, iso-C4, n-C4, iso-C5, n-C5, C6, C7, and C8. If nothing is selected, then all component volumes are reported per the analysis.

- **Min Component to Report** - Analysis on a sample may include lighter components such as C1 and C2. When the component volumes are reported on a printed ticket, the product may dictate that everything below a certain component be reported as that component. For instance on propane, analysis may include C2 for accurate component balancing, but all component volumes will be reported as C3. Setting the min component to report to C3 will cause the component volume from C2 to be reported as C3 component volume. FLOWCAL lumps these values together into a single value for viewing in the Components tab in the volume editor and the ticket editor and also for display on net Allowable ticket reports. Options for Min Component to Report are C1, C2, C3, iso-C4, n-C4, iso-C5, n-C5, and C6. If nothing is selected, then all component volumes are reported per the analysis. The rolling of components into a higher component is done after net allowable rules, if any are specified, have been applied.

- **Roll Ethylene into C2** - When checked, any component volume calculated from ethylene in the analysis is reported as C2 component volume. When the min component to report to is higher than C2, then ethylene volume is rolled into the minimum component. This option is only available when the Min Component to Report is set to C1 or C2.

- **Roll Propylene into C3** - When checked, any component volume calculated from propylene in the analysis is reported as C3 component volume. When the max component to report to is C2 or C3, then propylene volume is rolled into the maximum component. This option is only available when the Min Component to Report is set to C1, C2 or C3 and the Max Component to report is C4 or higher.

- **Roll Butylenes into C4** - When checked, any component volume calculated from butylenes in the analysis is reported as C4 component volume. When the max component to report to is higher than C4, then butylenes volume is rolled into the minimum component. This option is only available when the Max Component to Report is set to C5, C6, C7 or C8.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Aliases">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Product Aliases</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Aliases">

When setting up a product in FLOWCAL, the user must set a product code. This code is then used to map a product during import to a product in FLOWCAL. Potentially, each flow computer or data source has different codes for the same product.

**Example:** The user may have one system where demethanized mix is set up with a code of Y, whereas in another system demethanized mix is set up with a code of YGRADE. To accommodate this, FLOWCAL allows specification of product Aliases. Demethanized mix could be set up with a product code of Y and an alias of YGRADE or vice versa.

<div class="procedure">

Managing product aliases:

1.  To add an alias, click **New** below the Aliases section.
2.  Type in the name of a unique product alias in pop-up box. Click **OK** to add it.
3.  To remove an alias, highlight the Alias and click **Delete** below the Aliases section.
4.  To modify an existing alias, highlight it and click **Edit** below the Aliases section.

Each alias product ID can only belong to one product. An alias cannot be used on more than one product or be used as a product code on another product.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="C+">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />C+ Type “Apply Extended As” Rules</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="C+">

In the Quality Source Analysis Editor, if the “Has Extended Analysis” option is selected, FLOWCAL will follow the Apply Extended As value defined under Product \> Purity Product Options.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Full Analysis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

If a sample contains a full analysis (220 components) that goes out to C10, and the “Apply Extended As” option in any of the three places listed above is set to C6+, FLOWCAL will sum the values from C6 to C10 and apply the sum to C6. FLOWCAL will also apply the C6+ extended characteristics.

</div>

If the “Has Extended Analysis” option is not selected, FLOWCAL will apply the sample as it is given on the source and will apply the extended characteristics for the highest component that has a value. If the highest component that has a value is less that C6, the C6+ extended characteristics will be applied.

</div>
